<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Foreign Currency and Market Risk</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><!--EFPlaceholder-->We have direct operations in the United States, Canada, Western Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Singapore and South Africa, and we conduct additional business through distributors in Latin America, the Middle East, Eastern Europe and Asia.&#160;&#160;Our foreign operations are measured in their applicable local currencies.&#160;&#160;As a result, our financial results could be affected by factors such as changes in foreign currency exchange rates or weak economic conditions in the foreign markets in which we have operations.&#160;&#160;Exposure to these fluctuations is managed primarily through the use of natural hedges, whereby funding obligations and assets are both managed in the applicable local currency.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">KCI faces transactional currency exposures when its foreign subsidiaries enter into transactions denominated in currencies other than their local currency.&#160;&#160;These nonfunctional currency exposures relate primarily to existing intercompany receivables and payables arising from intercompany purchases of manufactured products.&#160;&#160;KCI enters into foreign currency exchange contracts to mitigate the impact of currency fluctuations on transactions and anticipated cash flows denominated in nonfunctional currencies, thereby limiting risk that would otherwise result from changes in exchange rates.&#160;&#160;The periods of the foreign currency exchange contracts correspond to the periods of the exposed transactions and anticipated cash flows but generally do not extend beyond 12 months.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2010, we had outstanding foreign currency exchange contracts to sell or purchase approximately $92.1 million of various currencies.&#160;&#160;Based on our overall transactional currency rate exposure, movements in the currency rates will not materially affect our financial condition.&#160;&#160;We are exposed to credit loss in the event of nonperformance by counterparties on their outstanding foreign currency exchange contracts.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">International operations reported operating profit of $106.3 million for 2010.&#160;&#160;We estimate that a 10% fluctuation in the value of the U.S. dollar relative to these foreign currencies as of and for the 2010 would change our net earnings for the period by approximately $10.0 million.&#160;&#160;Our analysis does not consider the implications that such fluctuations could have on the overall economic activity that could exist in such an environment in the United States or the foreign countries or on the results of operations of our foreign entities.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 1.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(a)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Principles of Consolidation</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The consolidated financial statements presented herein include the accounts of Kinetic Concepts,&#160;Inc., together with its consolidated subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;All inter-company balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.&#160;&#160;The consolidated entity is referred to herein as "KCI."&#160;&#160;The accompanying audited consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221; or &#8220;the Codification&#8221;) and with the instructions to Form 10-K and Article 10 of Regulation S-X.&#160;&#160;Certain prior period amounts have been reclassified to conform to the 2010 presentation.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have three reportable operating segments which correspond to our business units:&#160;&#160;Active Healing Solutions&#8482; (&#8220;AHS&#8221;); LifeCell; and Therapeutic Support Systems (&#8220;TSS&#8221;).&#160;&#160;We have two primary geographic regions for which we provide supplemental information:&#160;&#160;North America, which is comprised principally of the United States and includes Canada, Puerto Rico and Latin America; and EMEA/APAC, which is comprised principally of Europe and includes the Middle East, Africa and the Asia Pacific region.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">KCI has historically presented shared-service support costs associated with our international subsidiaries within rental expenses.&#160;&#160;We have reclassified these costs to SG&amp;A for each of the periods presented.&#160;&#160;The reclassification was enabled through the implementation of a global financial consolidation and reporting application that has allowed us to better capture certain international expenses associated with general and administrative activities.&#160;&#160;This reclassification increased our previously-reported gross profit, but it did not have any impact on previously-reported operating earnings or net earnings.&#160;&#160;We believe that this presentation is more consistent with our current practice for the reporting of global shared-service support costs and, therefore, provides more comparable financial information.&#160;&#160;The adjusted balances by year are summarized below (in thousands):</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">KCI is a leading global medical technology company devoted to the discovery, development, manufacture and marketing of innovative, high-technology therapies and products that have been designed to leverage the body&#8217;s ability to heal, thus improving clinical outcomes while helping to reduce the overall cost of patient care.&#160;&#160;We have an infrastructure designed to meet the specific needs of medical professionals and patients across all healthcare settings, including acute care hospitals, extended care organizations and patients&#8217; homes, both in the United States and abroad.&#160;&#160;We design, manufacture, market and service a wide range of proprietary products that can improve clinical outcomes and can help reduce the overall cost of patient care.&#160;&#160;Our AHS systems incorporate our proprietary V.A.C. Therapy technology, which is clinically-proven to promote wound healing through unique mechanisms of action, and to speed recovery times while reducing the overall cost of treating patients with complex wounds.&#160;&#160;Our LifeCell products include tissue-based products for use in reconstructive, orthopedic and urogynecologic surgical procedures to repair soft tissue defects.&#160;&#160;Our TSS business includes specialty hospital beds, mattress replacement systems and overlays, which are designed to address pulmonary complications associated with influenza, acute respiratory distress syndrome (&#8220;ARDS&#8221;) and immobility, to reduce or treat skin breakdown and assist caregivers in the safe and dignified handling of obese and morbidly obese patients.&#160;&#160;We have an infrastructure designed to meet the specific needs of medical professionals and patients across all healthcare settings, including acute care hospitals, extended care organizations and patients&#8217; homes, both in the United States and abroad.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have direct operations in the United States, Canada, Western Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Singapore, Hong Kong and South Africa, and we conduct additional business through distributors in Latin America, the Middle East, Eastern Europe and Asia.&#160;&#160;We manage our business in three reportable operating segments which correspond to our three business units:&#160;&#160;AHS, LifeCell, and TSS.&#160;&#160;We have operations in two primary geographic regions: North America, which is comprised principally of the United States and includes Canada, Puerto Rico and Latin America; and EMEA/APAC, which is comprised principally of Europe and includes the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific region.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Operations for our North America geographic region accounted for approximately 78.5%, 77.6% and 76.0% of our total revenue for 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;In the U.S. acute care setting, which accounted for approximately half of our North American revenue for the year ended December 31, 2010, we bill our customers directly for the rental and sale of our products.&#160;&#160;Also in the U.S. acute and extended care settings, we contract with both proprietary hospital groups and voluntary group purchasing organizations (&#8220;GPOs&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Proprietary hospital groups own all of the hospitals which they represent and, as a result, can ensure compliance with an executed national agreement.&#160;&#160;Voluntary GPOs negotiate contracts on behalf of member hospital organizations, but cannot ensure that their members will comply with the terms of an executed national agreement.&#160;&#160;Approximately 33.3%, 33.1% and 32.6% of our total revenue during 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively, was generated under national agreements with GPOs.&#160;&#160;During 2010, 2009 and 2008, we recorded approximately $176.9 million, $192.9&#160;million and $198.3&#160;million, respectively, in AHS and TSS revenues under contracts with Novation, LLC, our largest single GPO relationship.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In the U.S. homecare setting, where our revenue comes predominantly from our NPWT products, we provide products and services to patients in the home and bill third-party payers directly, such as Medicare and private insurance.&#160;&#160;During 2010, 2009 and 2008, we recorded revenue related to Medicare claims of approximately $163.6&#160;million, $155.2&#160;million and $170.4&#160;million, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In May 2008, we completed the acquisition of all the outstanding capital stock of LifeCell<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#8482;</font> Corporation for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $1.8 billion.&#160;&#160;LifeCell develops, processes and markets biological soft tissue repair products made from human or animal tissue.&#160;&#160;These products are used by surgeons to restore structure, function and physiology in a variety of reconstructive, orthopedic and urogynecologic surgical procedures.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">LifeCell revenue is generated primarily in the United States in the acute care setting on a direct billing basis.&#160;&#160;We market our regenerative and reconstructive acellular tissue matrix products for plastic reconstructive, general surgical and burn applications primarily to hospitals for use by general and plastic surgeons.&#160;&#160;Our primary tissue matrix products, AlloDerm and Strattice, are marketed through our direct sales and marketing organization.&#160;&#160;Our LifeCell sales representatives are responsible for interacting with plastic surgeons, general surgeons, head and neck surgeons, and trauma/acute care surgeons to educate them on the use and potential benefits of our tissue matrix products.&#160;&#160;We also participate in numerous national fellowship programs, national and international conferences and trade shows, and sponsor medical education symposiums.&#160;&#160;Our tissue matrix products for orthopedic and urogynecologic procedures are marketed through independent sales agents and distributors.&#160;&#160;These products include GRAFTJACKET, for orthopedic applications and lower extremity wounds; AlloCraft DBM, for bone grafting procedures; Repliform TRM, for urogynecologic surgical procedures; and Conexa, for rotator cuff tissue repairs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<td valign="bottom" width="13%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;&#160; 1%</font></td>
<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left">&#160;</td>
</tr></table>
</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The domestic TPP reimbursement process requires extensive documentation, which has had the effect of slowing both the billing and cash collection cycles relative to the rest of the business, and therefore, could increase total accounts receivable.&#160;&#160;Because of the extensive documentation required and the requirement to settle a claim with the primary payer prior to billing the secondary and/or patient portion of the claim, the collection period for a claim in our homecare business may, in some cases, extend beyond one year prior to full settlement of the claim.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We utilize a combination of factors in evaluating the collectibility of our accounts receivable.&#160;&#160;For unbilled receivables, we establish reserves to allow for expected denied or uncollectible items.&#160;&#160;In addition, items that remain unbilled for more than a specified period of time, or beyond an established billing window, are reserved against revenue.&#160;&#160;For billed receivables, we generally establish reserves using a combination of factors including historic adjustment rates for credit memos and cancelled transactions, historical collection experience, and the length of time receivables have been outstanding.&#160;&#160;The reserve rates vary by payer group.&#160;&#160;In addition, we record specific reserves for bad debt when we become aware of a customer's inability or refusal to satisfy its debt obligations, such as in the event of a bankruptcy filing.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(h)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Inventories</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 20pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">AHS and TSS inventories</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Inventories are stated at the lower of cost (first-in, first-out) or market (net realizable value).&#160;&#160;Costs include material, labor, distribution and manufacturing overhead costs.&#160;&#160;Inventory expected to be converted into equipment for short-term rental is reclassified to property, plant and equipment.&#160;&#160;We review our inventory balances monthly for excess sale products or obsolete inventory levels.&#160;&#160;Inventory quantities of sale-only products in excess of anticipated demand are considered excess and are reserved at 100%.&#160;&#160;For rental products, we review both product usage and product life cycle to classify inventory as active, discontinued or obsolete.&#160;&#160;Obsolescence reserve balances are established on an increasing basis from 0% for active, high-demand products to 100% for obsolete products.&#160;&#160;The reserve is reviewed, and if necessary, adjustments are made on a monthly basis.&#160;&#160;We rely on historical information and production planning forecasts to support our reserve and utilize management's business judgment for "high risk" items, such as products that have a fixed shelf life.&#160;&#160;Once the value of inventory is reduced, we do not adjust the reserve balance until the inventory is sold or otherwise disposed.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our manufacturing plant in Athlone, Ireland currently manufactures our V.A.C.Via, Prevena, ABThera and other V.A.C. Therapy units for our global markets.&#160;&#160;Our Ireland plant also manufactures certain disposable supplies, on a high-volume automation line, which have historically been supplied by Avail Medical Products, Inc. (&#8220;Avail&#8221;), a subsidiary of Flextronics International Ltd.&#160;&#160;We plan to continue leveraging our existing infrastructure and manufacturing capabilities within our Athlone plant and expand internal production in the future.&#160;&#160;In 2007, we entered into a contract manufacturing agreement with Avail, which has a term of five years through November 2012 and may be renewed by agreement of both parties.&#160;&#160;Under this agreement, we have title to the raw materials used to manufacture our disposable supplies and retain title of all disposables inventory throughout the manufacturing process.&#160;&#160;The terms of this agreement provide that key indicators be provided to us that would alert us to any inability of Avail to perform under the agreement.&#160;&#160;Approximately 22.1%, 22.6% and 24.1% of our total revenue for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively, was generated from the sale of disposable supplies within our AHS business.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 20pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">LifeCell inventories</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Inventories are stated at the lower of cost or market, with cost being determined on a first-in, first-out basis.&#160;&#160;Inventories on hand include the cost of materials, freight, direct labor and manufacturing overhead.&#160;&#160;We record a provision for excess and obsolete inventory based primarily on inventory quantities on hand, the historical product sales and estimated forecast of future product demand and production requirements.&#160;&#160;In addition, we record a provision for tissue that will not meet tissue standards based on historic rejection rates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(i)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Vendor Rebates</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We may receive consideration from vendors in the normal course of business in the form of rebates of purchase price paid.&#160;&#160;Our policy for accounting for these funds is in accordance with the &#8220;Revenue Recognition&#8221; Topic of the FASB Accounting Standards Codification.&#160;&#160;Funds are recognized as a reduction of cost of sales and inventory if the funds are a reduction of the price for the vendor&#8217;s products.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(j)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Long-Lived Assets</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Property, plant and equipment are stated at cost. Betterments, which extend the useful life of the equipment, are capitalized.&#160;&#160;Software development costs for internal use are capitalized pursuant to the &#8220;Intangibles-Goodwill and Other&#8221; Topic of the Codification.&#160;&#160;Debt issuance costs at December 31, 2010 represent fees and other direct costs incurred in connection with our borrowings.&#160;&#160;These amounts are capitalized and amortized using the effective interest method over the contractual term of the borrowing.&#160;&#160;During 2008, we capitalized $60.7 million related to the completion of our acquisition financing.&#160;&#160;(See Note 2.)&#160;&#160;Other assets consist principally of patents, trademarks, long-term investments and our investment in assets subject to leveraged leases.&#160;&#160;Patents and trademarks are amortized over the estimated useful life of the respective asset using the straight-line method unless another method is determined to be more appropriate.&#160;&#160;Patent and trademark costs associated with products for which we are no longer pursuing development are written-off to expense.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Depreciation on property, plant and equipment is calculated on the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives (20 to 30&#160;years for buildings and between three and seven years for most of our other property and equipment) of the assets. Amortization for leasehold improvements is taken over the shorter of the estimated useful life of the asset or over the remaining lease term.&#160;&#160;Depreciation expense for 2010, 2009 and 2008 was $94.7 million, $99.3 million and $97.1 million, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(k)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Goodwill represents the excess purchase price over the fair value of net assets acquired. Goodwill is tested at least annually by reporting unit for impairment, or more frequently when events or changes in circumstances indicate that the asset might be impaired. For indefinite lived intangible assets, impairment is tested by comparing the carrying value of the asset to the fair value of the reporting unit. KCI defines its reporting units at the same level as our segments disclosed in Note 15: AHS, LifeCell and TSS. Goodwill was tested for impairment during the fourth quarter of 2010 and we determined that the estimated fair values substantially exceeded the carrying values for all of our reporting units and therefore no impairment write down was required.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The fair value of each reporting unit was primarily determined using discounted cash flow models. Significant assumptions included risk-based discount rates ranging from 11% to 15%, estimated growth rates based on KCI&#8217;s long-range planning model and terminal values of each reporting unit based on a growth rate of 3.5% after the 10th year. Goodwill arising from the LifeCell purchase was allocated to the applicable reporting units based on the discounted projected benefit received by that reporting unit.&#160;&#160;(See Note 4.)</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Identifiable intangible assets include developed technology, customer relationships, tradenames and patents.&#160;&#160;We amortize our identifiable intangible assets over 2 to 20&#160;years, depending on the estimated economic or contractual life of the individual asset.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(l)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income Taxes</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Deferred income taxes are accounted for using the asset and liability method of accounting for income taxes, whereby deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized based on the tax effects of temporary differences between the financial statements and the tax bases of assets and liabilities, as measured by current enacted tax rates. &#160;When appropriate, we evaluate the need for a valuation allowance to reduce our deferred tax assets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A liability is recorded for unrecognized tax benefits resulting from uncertain tax positions taken or expected to be taken in a tax return. &#160;We recognize interest and penalties, if any, related to unrecognized tax benefits in income tax expense.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2010, deferred tax assets recorded by KCI increased from 2009. &#160;We have established a valuation allowance to reduce deferred tax assets associated with foreign net operating losses, certain foreign deferred tax assets and state research and development credits to an amount whose realization is more likely than not. &#160;We anticipate that the reversal of existing taxable temporary differences and future income will provide sufficient taxable income to realize the tax benefit of the remaining deferred tax assets; therefore we have not provided a valuation allowance.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The effective income tax rate for 2010 was 28.0% compared to 31.6% in 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(m)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Net Earnings Per Share</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Basic net earnings per share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;) is computed by dividing net earnings by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for the period.&#160;&#160;Diluted EPS reflects the potential dilution that could occur if securities or other contracts to issue common stock were exercised or converted into common stock or resulted in the issuance of common stock.&#160;&#160;The dilutive effect is calculated based on the average share price for each fiscal period using the treasury stock method.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(n)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Royalties</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We pay royalties for the right to market many of our medical devices.&#160;&#160;Royalties are based on applicable revenue and recognized in the period that the related revenue is earned.&#160;&#160;Royalties related to rental revenue are included in rental expense.&#160;&#160;Royalties on sales revenue are included in cost of sales.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(o)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Self-Insurance</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We self-insure certain employee benefit and casualty insurance risks.&#160;&#160;Our group medical plan for U.S. employees is a qualified self-insured plan subject to specific stop loss insurance coverage.&#160;&#160;Our short-term disability plan for U.S. based employees is self-insured.&#160;&#160;The Texas Employee Injury Benefit Plan is self-insured subject to a $750,000 per occurrence retention. Our casualty insurance program has a $750,000 deductible for workers&#8217; compensation, auto liability, and general liability.&#160;&#160;Our products liability program has a $500,000 self-insurance retention.&#160;&#160;Our group life and accidental death and dismemberment plan and our long-term disability plan are all fully insured. We fully accrue our retained loss liabilities, including claims incurred but not reported.&#160;&#160;&#160;Based on historical trends, we believe our accruals for retained losses are adequate to cover future losses.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(p)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Derivative Financial Instruments and Fair Value Measurements</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We use derivative financial instruments to manage the economic impact of fluctuations in interest rates.&#160;&#160;We do not use financial instruments for speculative or trading purposes.&#160;&#160;Periodically, we enter into interest rate protection agreements to modify the interest characteristics of our outstanding debt.&#160;&#160;We designated our interest rate swap agreements as cash flow hedge instruments.&#160;&#160;Each interest rate swap is designated as a hedge of interest payments associated with specific principal balances and terms of our debt obligations.&#160;&#160;These agreements involve the exchange of amounts based on variable interest rates, for amounts based on fixed interest rates over the life of the agreement, without an exchange of the notional amount upon which the payments are based.&#160;&#160;The differential to be paid or received, as interest rates change, is accrued and recognized as an adjustment to interest expense related to the debt.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also use derivative financial instruments to manage the economic impact of fluctuations in currency exchange rates on our intercompany balances and corresponding cash flows and to manage our transactional currency exposures when our foreign subsidiaries enter into transactions denominated in currencies other than their local currency.&#160;&#160;We enter into foreign currency exchange contracts to manage these economic risks.&#160;&#160;These contracts are not designated as hedges; as such, we recognize the fair value of these instruments as an asset or liability with income or expense recognized in the current period.&#160;&#160;Gains and losses resulting from the foreign currency fluctuations impact on transactional exposures are included in foreign currency gain (loss) in our consolidated statements of earnings.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As required, all derivative instruments are recorded on the balance sheet at fair value.&#160;&#160;The fair values of our interest rate swap agreements and foreign currency exchange contracts are determined based on inputs that are readily available in public markets or can be derived from information available in publicly-quoted markets, which represent level 2 inputs as defined by the Codification.&#160;&#160;We estimate the effectiveness of our interest rate swap agreements utilizing the hypothetical derivative method.&#160;&#160;Under this method, the fair value of the actual interest rate swap agreement is compared to the fair value of a hypothetical swap agreement that has the same critical terms as the portion of the loan being hedged.&#160;&#160;Changes in the effective portion of the fair value of the remaining interest rate swap agreement will be recognized in other comprehensive income, net of tax, until the hedged item is recognized into earnings.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(q)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Foreign Currency Translation and Transaction Gains and Losses</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The functional currency for the majority of our foreign operations is the applicable local currency.&#160;&#160;The translation of the applicable foreign currencies into U.S. dollars is performed for balance sheet accounts using the exchange rates in effect at the balance sheet date and for revenue and expense accounts using a weighted average exchange rate during the period. Gains and losses resulting from the foreign currency translations are included in accumulated other comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;Transaction gains and losses, such as those resulting from the settlement of nonfunctional currency receivables or payables, including intercompany balances, are included in foreign currency gain (loss) in our consolidated statements of earnings.&#160;&#160;Additionally, payable and receivable balances denominated in nonfunctional currencies are marked-to-market at month-end, and the gain or loss is recognized in our consolidated statements of earnings.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(r)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Concentration of Credit Risk</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">KCI has a concentration of credit risk with financial institutions related to its derivative instruments and the note hedge described in Note 5.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, Bank of America and JP Morgan Chase collectively held equity hedges related to our convertible note hedge, as described in Note 5, in notional amounts totaling $352.9 million.&#160;&#160;Bank of America was also the counterparty on some of our interest rate protection agreements and our foreign currency exchange contracts in notional amounts totaling $35.5 million and $6.2 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;Additionally, JP Morgan Chase was a counterparty on some of our foreign currency exchange contracts in notional amounts totaling $5.0 million.&#160;&#160;We use master netting agreements with our derivative counterparties to reduce our risk and use multiple counterparties to reduce our concentration of credit risk.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(s)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Collaborative Arrangements</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In September 2010, LifeCell entered into an exclusive sales and marketing agreement with Novadaq<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#174; </font>Technologies, Inc. (&#8220;Novadaq&#8221;) for the distribution of&#160;&#160;Novadaq's SPY<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#174;</font> Intraoperative Perfusion Assessment System in North American surgical markets.&#160;&#160;LifeCell will provide market development and commercialization activities, including professional education, clinical support, reimbursement and sales distribution.&#160;&#160;Novadaq will continue to be responsible for manufacturing, field service and research and development.&#160;&#160;We recognize revenue for transactions under this agreement in accordance with the &#8220;Collaborative Arrangements&#8221; topic of the Codification.&#160;&#160;Transactions under this agreement were not material for the year ended December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(t)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Share-based Compensation</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We measure and recognize share-based compensation expense over the estimated service period for all share-based payment awards, including stock options, restricted stock awards and restricted stock units based on estimated fair values on the date of grant.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">KCI has elected to use the Black-Scholes model to estimate the fair value of option grants.&#160;&#160;We believe that the use of the Black-Scholes model meets the fair value measurement objective and reflects all substantive characteristics of the instruments being valued.&#160;&#160;Estimates of fair value are not intended to predict actual future events or the value ultimately realized by employees who receive share-based compensation awards, and subsequent events will not affect the original estimates of fair value made by us.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The expected stock volatility is based on historical volatilities of KCI and other similar entities.&#160;&#160;The expected dividend yield is 0% as we have historically not paid cash dividends on our common stock.&#160;&#160;The risk-free interest rates for periods within the contractual life of the option are based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of grant.&#160;&#160;We have chosen to estimate expected life using the simplified method as permitted rather than using our own historical expected life as there has not been sufficient history since we completed our initial public offering to allow us to better estimate this variable.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(u)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Research and Development</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The focus of our research and development program has been to invest in clinical studies and the development of new advanced wound healing systems, products and dressings.&#160;&#160;This includes the development of new and synergistic technologies across the continuum of wound care including tissue regeneration, preservation and repair, new applications of negative pressure technology, as well as upgrading and expanding our surface technologies in our TSS business and the leveraging of our core understanding of biological tissues in order to develop biosurgery products in our LifeCell business.&#160;&#160;The types of costs classified as research and development expense include salaries of technical staff, consultant costs, facilities and utilities costs related to offices occupied by technical staff, depreciation on equipment and facilities used by technical staff, supplies and materials for research and development and outside services such as prototype development and testing and third-party research and development costs.&#160;&#160;Expenditures for research and development, including expenses related to clinical studies, are expensed as incurred.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(v)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Shipping and Handling</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We include shipping and handling costs in rental expense and cost of sales, as appropriate.&#160;&#160;Shipping and handling costs on sales products recovered from customers of $4.1 million, $4.3&#160;million and $4.2&#160;million for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively, are included in sales revenue for these periods.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(w)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Taxes Collected from Customers and Remitted to Governmental Units</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Taxes assessed by a government authority that are directly imposed on a revenue producing transaction between KCI and our customers, including but not limited to sales taxes, use taxes and value added taxes, are accounted for on a net (excluded from revenues and costs) basis.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(x)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Advertising Expenses</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Advertising costs are expensed as incurred.&#160;&#160;Advertising expenses were $12.9 million, $13.3 million and $12.1 million for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(y)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Seasonality</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Historically, we have experienced a seasonal slowing of AHS unit growth beginning in the fourth quarter and continuing into the first quarter, which we believe has been caused by year-end clinical treatment patterns, such as the postponement of elective surgeries and increased discharges of individuals from the acute care setting around the winter holidays.&#160;&#160;LifeCell has also historically experienced a similar seasonal slowing of sales in the third quarter of each year.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div id="FTR">

</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(z)&#160;&#160;&#160;Legal Proceedings and Other Loss Contingencies</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are subject to various legal proceedings, many involving routine litigation incidental to our business.&#160;&#160;The outcome of any legal proceeding is not within our complete control, is often difficult to predict and is resolved over very long periods of time.&#160;&#160;Estimating probable losses associated with any legal proceedings or other loss contingencies is very complex and requires the analysis of many factors including assumptions about potential actions by third parties.&#160;&#160;Loss contingencies are disclosed when there is at least a reasonable possibility that a loss has been incurred and are recorded as liabilities in the consolidated financial statements when it is both (1)&#160;probable or known that a liability has been incurred and (2)&#160;the amount of the loss is reasonably estimable.&#160;&#160;If the reasonable estimate of the loss is a range and no amount within the range is a better estimate, the minimum amount of the range is recorded as a liability.&#160;&#160;If a loss contingency is not probable or cannot be reasonably estimated, a liability is not recorded in the consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">(aa)</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Recently Adopted Accounting Principles</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In October 2009, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update No. 2009-13 &#8220;Revenue Recognition (Topic 605): Multiple-Deliverable Revenue Arrangements &#8211; a consensus of the FASB Emerging Issues Task Force.&#8221;&#160;&#160;This update provides amendments to the criteria for separating consideration in multiple-deliverable arrangements.&#160;&#160;This update also significantly expands the disclosures related to a company&#8217;s multiple-deliverable revenue arrangements.&#160;&#160;The amendments in this update were effective for KCI for revenue arrangements entered into or materially modified beginning January 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this update did not have a material impact on our results of operations or our financial position.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTE 2.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Acquisition</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On May 27, 2008, we completed the acquisition of all the outstanding capital stock of LifeCell Corporation (&#8220;LifeCell&#8221;) for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $1.8 billion.&#160;&#160;The purchase price consisted of $1.7 billion of cash paid to acquire the outstanding common stock of LifeCell, at a price of $51.00 per share, $83.0 million in fair value of assumed vested stock options, restricted stock awards and restricted stock units, and $20.7 million of acquisition related transaction costs, which primarily consisted of fees incurred for financial advisory and legal services.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The LifeCell acquisition was accounted for as a business combination using the purchase method and, accordingly, the fair value of the net assets acquired and the results of operations for LifeCell have been included in KCI&#8217;s consolidated financial statements from the acquisition date forward.&#160;&#160;The allocation of the total purchase price to LifeCell&#8217;s net tangible and identifiable intangible assets was based on their estimated fair values as of the acquisition date.&#160;&#160;The excess of the purchase price over the identifiable intangible and net tangible assets, in the amount of $1.3 billion, was allocated to goodwill.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The results of LifeCell&#8217;s operations since the acquisition date have been included in our consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;The following table reflects the unaudited pro forma consolidated results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2008, as though the acquisition of LifeCell had occurred as of January 1, 2008 (dollars in thousands, except per share data):</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Senior Credit Facility</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In May 2008, we entered into a $1.3 billion senior secured credit facility due May 2013.&#160;&#160;The senior credit facility consists of a $1.0 billion term loan facility and a $300.0 million revolving credit facility.&#160;&#160;Up to $75.0 million of the revolving credit facility is available for letters of credit and up to $25.0 million of the revolving credit facility is available for swing-line loans.&#160;&#160;Amounts available under the revolving credit facility are available for borrowing and reborrowing until maturity.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010 and 2009, we had no revolving credit loans outstanding and had outstanding letters of credit in the aggregate amount of $11.6 million and $11.4 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;The resulting availability under the revolving credit facility was $288.4 million and $288.6 million at December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Interest</font>. Amounts outstanding under the senior credit facility bear interest at a rate equal to the base rate (defined as the higher of Bank of America's prime rate or 50 basis points above the federal funds rate) or the Eurocurrency rate (the LIBOR rate), in each case plus an applicable margin.&#160;&#160;The applicable margin varies in reference to our consolidated leverage ratio and ranges from 1.75% to 3.50% in the case of loans based on the Eurocurrency rate and 0.75% to 2.50% in the case of loans based on the base rate.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, our nominal interest rate on borrowings under the senior credit facility was 4.500%.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We may choose base rate or Eurocurrency pricing and may elect interest periods of 1, 2, 3 or 6 months for the Eurocurrency borrowings. Interest on base rate borrowings is payable quarterly in arrears.&#160;&#160;Interest on Eurocurrency borrowings is payable at the end of each applicable interest period or every three months in the case of interest periods in excess of three months.&#160;&#160;Interest on all past due amounts will accrue at 2.00% over the applicable rate.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Collateral. </font>The senior credit facility is secured by a first priority lien and security interest in (a) substantially all shares of capital stock and intercompany debt of each of our present and future subsidiaries (limited in the case of certain subsidiaries to 65% of the voting stock of such entity) and (b) substantially all of our present and future real property (with a value in excess of $10 million individually), and the present and future assets of our subsidiaries that are and will be guarantors under the senior credit facility.&#160;&#160;The security interest is subject to some exceptions and permitted liens.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Guarantors. </font>Our obligations under the senior credit facility are guaranteed by each of our direct and indirect 100% owned subsidiaries, other than foreign subsidiaries or subsidiaries whose only assets are investments in foreign subsidiaries.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Maturity</font>. The senior credit facility matures on May 19, 2013.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Voluntary Prepayments</font>. We may prepay, in full or in part, borrowings under the senior credit facility without premium or penalty, subject to minimum prepayment amount and increment limitations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Mandatory Repayments</font>. We must make periodic prepayments of an aggregate principal amount of the term loans equal to (i) 100% of the net cash proceeds of certain dispositions of property, (ii) 100% of the net cash proceeds of the issuance or incurrence of certain indebtedness, (iii) 50% of the net cash proceeds received from certain equity issuances, and (iv) 50% (or a reduced percentage determined in reference to our consolidated leverage ratio) of our domestic excess cash flow.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Representations</font>. The senior credit facility contains representations generally customary for similar facilities and transactions.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

It will be an event of default if we permit any of the following:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>

</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Events of Default</font>. </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The senior credit facility contains events of default including, but not limited to, failure to pay principal or interest, breaches of representations and warranties, violations of affirmative or negative covenants, cross-defaults to other indebtedness, a bankruptcy or similar proceeding being instituted by or against us, rendering of certain monetary judgments against us, impairments of loan documentation or security, changes of ownership or operating control, defaults with respect to certain ERISA obligations and termination of material contracts.</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of December 31, 2010 and 2009, we were in compliance with all covenants under the senior credit agreement.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In January 2011, we entered into a new credit agreement which was used to refinance existing debt under the prior senior credit facility and will also be used for general corporate purposes.&#160;&#160;The new credit agreement provides for (i) a $550.0 million term A facility that matures in January 2016, and (ii)&#160;a $650.0 million revolving credit facility that matures in January 2016, which represents a $350.0 million increase from our previous revolving credit facility.&#160;&#160;The Company also has the right at any time to increase its borrowings under the new credit agreement by an aggregate additional amount up to $500.0 million. &#160;(See Note 17.)</font></div>

</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">3.25% Convertible Senior Notes</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In 2008, we issued $690 million aggregate principal amount of 3.25% convertible senior notes due 2015 (the &#8220;Convertible Notes&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The notes are governed by the terms of an indenture dated as of April 21, 2008 (the &#8220;Indenture&#8221;).</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Principal Amount. </font>At December 31, 2010, $690.0 million in aggregate principal amount of the notes was outstanding.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Interest</font>. The coupon on the notes is 3.25% per year on the principal amount. Interest began accruing from April 21, 2008, and is payable semi-annually in arrears on April 15 and October 15 of each year, beginning October 15, 2008.&#160;&#160;For 2010, 2009 and 2008 we recorded interest related to the contractual interest coupon rate totaling $22.4 million, $22.4 million and $15.6 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;Additionally, based on our estimated non-convertible borrowing rate of 7.78%, we recorded approximately $21.3 million, $19.7 million and $12.8 million of additional non-cash interest expense related to the amortization of the discount on the Convertible Notes for 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Guarantor. </font>Our wholly-owned subsidiary, KCI USA, Inc. (the &#8220;Subsidiary Guarantor&#8221;),&#160;&#160;has guaranteed the principal and interest payable under the notes on a contractually subordinated basis to its secured guarantee of our new credit facility and any credit facilities we enter into in the future.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Ranking. </font>The Convertible Notes are senior unsecured obligations, and rank (i)&#160;senior to any of our future indebtedness that is expressly subordinated to the notes; (ii)&#160;equally to any future senior subordinated debt; and (iii)&#160;effectively junior to any secured indebtedness to the extent of the value of the assets securing such indebtedness. In addition, the notes are structurally junior to (i)&#160;all existing and future indebtedness and other liabilities incurred by our subsidiaries and (ii)&#160;preferred stock issued by our subsidiaries, except that in the case of the guarantee of the principal and interest on the notes by the Subsidiary Guarantor, such guarantee will be (a)&#160;effectively subordinated to all of the Subsidiary Guarantor&#8217;s secured debt to the extent of the value of the assets securing such debt, (b)&#160;contractually subordinated to its secured guarantee of our new credit facility and any credit facilities we enter into in the future, (c)&#160;pari passu with all of its other senior indebtedness, and (d)&#160;senior to all of its indebtedness that is expressly subordinated in right of payment to the subsidiary guarantee and all of its preferred stock outstanding.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Maturity</font>. The Convertible Notes will mature on April 15, 2015, unless previously converted or repurchased in accordance with their terms prior to such date.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the notes are classified as a non-current liability.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Redemption</font>. The Convertible Notes are not redeemable by us prior to the maturity date, but the holders may require us to repurchase the notes at 100% of the principal amount of the notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest, following a &#8220;fundamental change&#8221; (as defined in the Indenture).</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Conversion.</font> Holders of the Convertible Notes may convert their notes at their option on any day prior to the close of business on the business day immediately preceding October 15, 2014 only if one or more of the following conditions is satisfied:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 40pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(1)&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">during any fiscal quarter commencing after June 30, 2008, if the last reported sale price of our common stock for at least 20 trading days in the period of 30 consecutive trading days ending on the last trading day of the preceding fiscal quarter is greater than or equal to 130% of the conversion price of the notes in effect on each applicable trading day;</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 40pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(2)&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">during the five business day period following any five consecutive trading day period in which the trading price for the notes (per $1,000 principal amount of the notes) for each such trading day was less than 98% of the last reported sale price of our common stock on such date multiplied by the applicable conversion rate; or</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

</td>
<td>
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">if we make certain significant distributions to holders of our common stock or enter into specified corporate transactions. The notes are convertible, regardless of whether any of the foregoing conditions has been satisfied, on or after October&#160;15, 2014 at any time prior to the close of business on the third scheduled trading day immediately preceding the stated maturity date.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Upon conversion, holders will receive cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted and shares of our common stock in respect of the remainder, if any, of our conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted.&#160;&#160;The initial conversion rate for the notes is 19.4764 shares of our common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which is equivalent to an initial conversion price of approximately $51.34 per share of common stock and represents a 27.5% conversion premium over the last reported sale price of our common stock on April 15, 2008, which was $40.27 per share.&#160;&#160;The conversion rate and the conversion price are subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events, such as distributions of dividends or stock splits.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 20pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
